rationale: Obscure verb form, possibly Greek παράγω adapted to Lycopolitan, or a verb of cosmic passage. Context: subject is Father of Life and Mother of the Living (with First Man); object/direction is 'toward the mystery of the second worship.' Tentative; needs parallels.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ϣⲁϫⲉ. In the phrase ⲡⲓⲧⲟⲩ ⲛ-ⲥⲉⲭⲉ 'the five words' — the fivefold ritual formula by which the descending Mind greets his Church.

Verb of greeting/embracing, semantically paired with ⲡⲁⲥⲡⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ in line 33. Possibly cognate with ⲥⲱⲡ 'receive, take into one's bosom.' Used twice on this page (lines 26-27) for the Mind's greeting of his Church.
Lycopolitan = Sahidic ϩⲣⲟⲟⲩ 'voice.' Standard sound-noun, with 3pl suffix in line 12 ('their voice came to him').
Lycopolitan plural of ϩⲟⲉⲓⲙ 'wave.' Used cosmologically of the chaotic 'waves' of the war from which the First Man is rescued.
Greek loanword πόλεμος. Standard Manichaean term for the primordial cosmic war between Light and Darkness. Capitalized.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ/ⲡⲓⲥⲧⲓⲥ. Standard Coptic noun for 'faith, belief'; here the destination state of the elected/chosen one (line 30).
Lycopolitan ⲛⲁⲍⲙⲉ = Sahidic ⲛⲟⲩϩⲙ 'rescue, save.' With 3sg.m suffix in line 7.
Lycopolitan imperative of ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'sit'; ⲧ- as imperative prefix. Quotation of Ps 110:1 in line 13.

proposed_english: set on his feet / cause to stand
rationale: ⲥⲉⲍⲉ = Sahidic ⲥⲱϩⲉ 'stand'; with ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'on the feet of' = causative 'cause to stand, set upright before.' Cosmologically the First Man is set before the Father after rescue.
